value: Law No. 26 of 2007 Regulating the Relationship between Landlords and Tenants in the Emirate of Dubai.
note: English text is a translation; the Arabic text prevails. Amendments after publication were not reviewed.

value: All lease contracts under the law must be registered with RERA; courts and government bodies may not consider a dispute on an unregistered contract (art. 4(2)). Registration is done through the Ejari system, the Dubai REST app or an authorised trustee office.
source_publisher: Dubai Legislation Portal; Dubai Land Department

value: At renewal the maximum increase depends on how far rent is below the RERA average for similar units: 0 percent if up to 10 percent below; 5 percent if 11-20 percent below; 10 percent if 21-30 percent below; 15 percent if 31-40 percent below; 20 percent if more than 40 percent below (Decree No. 43 of 2013, art. 1). The decree applies to all landlords in Dubai including special zones such as the DIFC (art. 2).

The average rental value of similar units is determined under the Rent Index of Dubai approved by RERA (Decree 43/2013, art. 3); the Dubai Land Department Rental Index service calculates the average rent and permitted increase for an area.
source_publisher: Dubai Legislation Portal; Dubai Land Department

field: Notice of non-renewal or change of terms
value: A party who does not wish to renew, or wishes to amend terms, must notify the other at least 90 days before expiry unless the parties agree otherwise (art. 14).
